results.note: persist_missing_comparison (corroborate.py:277-289) calls persist_datapoint with the primary OKX Ok value before recording NOT_CORROBORATED. The test (tests/test_not_corroborated.py:79-93) asserts the mocked persist_datapoint was actually called with the Ok(78300.70) result, proving the primary value is stored regardless of the second venue's outcome.

run_live_corroboration returns the raw Error unmodified for an Error second-venue result (line 291-292) but returns a NotCorroboratedRecord for a missing/older bar. The test directly compares both paths in one test, and coinbase.py:31-40 confirms an HTTP 500 or request failure produces Error(reason=FETCH_FAILED), never Unavailable.

NotCorroboratedRecord (corroborate.py:39-48, slots=True) has no divergence_bps/tolerance_bps_at_write fields at all -- not set to 0 or None, simply absent from the type. Test asserts hasattr(...) is False for both, and the corroborations table's comparison_values_together CHECK constraint (migration 20260910120000, lines 28-39) enforces divergence_bps/tolerance_bps_at_write IS NULL when datapoint_b_id IS NULL, so the DB layer also refuses to store a fabricated zero.

corroboration_is_failure returns True only for Error. coinbase.py:61-64 returns Unavailable(reason=FETCH_FAILED) (not Error) when no closed candle exists for a quiet market, and test_no_closed_second_venue_bars_is_also_not_corroborated confirms that flows to NotCorroboratedRecord, not a switch-firing outcome, exercising the exact 'no ticks' shape described in the story.

record_not_corroborated requires a non-optional Reason and persists it in the 'reason' text column; the reused Reason enum (ingest/status.py:9-16) and its FETCH_FAILED value ('should exist, did not arrive ... empty after filtering', project-documents/11_Data_Model.md:41) is the exact vocabulary applied to both the Unavailable-second-venue and older-latest-candle paths (corroborate.py:293-294,312-313), so absence is never recorded without a reason.

note: All five criteria are backed by concrete code and assertion-bearing tests; the new corroborations migration schema (already in place) structurally enforces the value/absence distinction via CHECK constraints. One caveat worth flagging: corroboration_is_failure and run_live_corroboration are not called from any production entry point (ingest/heartbeat.py's run_ingestion still calls run_pipeline/fetch_btc_daily_close directly, not run_live_corroboration) — the dead-man's-switch semantics are proven only at the unit level, never wired into the actual switch-triggering code. This doesn't fail any criterion since all are declared method:test (not integration) and the tests match the criteria text as written, but it means the story's headline claim about the real dead-man's-switch remains unverified end-to-end.
